newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end down on overseas selling.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end down on overseas selling.

text.p: Shanghai B shares closed down on Tuesday on overseas selling with the market in a gloomy mood in the short term in the absense of positive news, brokers said.
The index fell 0.343 point or 0.68 percent to 50.059, on volume of 7.7 million shares worth $2.9 million. Of 41 B shares, 31 traded, with 14 down, 11 flat and six up.
Brokers said that market sentiment had worsened with the index falling below 50 points for a time during the day. It hit an intra-day low of 49.933 points later in the session.
"The index was pushed back above 50 points just ahead of closing thanks to some reluctant support buying, but it is difficult to improve recent poor sentiment," one trader said.
"The index is still on a downward track on increasing overseas selling, and the 48-point support level will be tested in the next few days," another broker said.
China Textile Machinery was the biggest loser, falling $0.010 or 9.09 percent to $0.100 on volume of 108,500 shares.
Heilongjiang Electric Power traded most on heavy liquidation selling from an overseas institution despite support by another institution, brokers said.
It shed $0.002 or 0.55 percent to $0.360 on volume of 1.8 million shares.
Shanghai A shares ended down with the market moving into consolidation, brokers said.
The A index edged down 1.791 points or 0.22 percent to 811.858 points, on volume of 257.8 million shares worth 2.4 billion yuan. The SSE 30 fell 6.123 points or 0.29 percent to 2081.517 points.
Chang An Information was the biggest loser, falling 0.35 yuan or 5.42 percent to 6.10 yuan on volume of 66,300 shares.
